 def load_historical_dashboard_data(
     config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
 ) -> dict[str, Any]:
     """Calculate historical application counts and observed label breakdowns."""
     settings = validate_config(config if config is not None else load_config())
     paths = get_project_paths(settings)
     frame = load_csv(paths.labeled_dataset)
     target_column = settings["dataset"]["target_column"]
     target_classes = settings["dataset"]["target_classes"]
     if target_column not in frame or frame[target_column].isna().any():
         raise DataValidationError("Historical dashboard target is missing or invalid")
 
     counts = frame[target_column].value_counts().reindex(target_classes, fill_value=0)
     if int(counts.sum()) != len(frame) or (counts <= 0).any():
         raise DataValidationError("Historical target counts do not match dataset rows")
     approval_count = int(counts["Y"])
     rejection_count = int(counts["N"])
     approval_by_area = (
         frame.groupby(["Property_Area", target_column], observed=False)
         .size()
         .unstack(fill_value=0)
         .reindex(columns=target_classes, fill_value=0)
         .rename(columns={"Y": "Y", "N": "N"})
         .rename_axis("Property_Area")
         .reset_index()
     )
     return {
         "application_count": int(len(frame)),
         "approval_count": approval_count,
         "rejection_count": rejection_count,
         "approval_rate": approval_count / len(frame),
         "rejection_rate": rejection_count / len(frame),
         "status_counts": counts.rename(index={"Y": "Approved", "N": "Rejected"}),
         "approval_by_area": approval_by_area,
         "source": str(paths.labeled_dataset),
         "target_column": target_column,
     }
 
 
 def _read_json(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
     try:
         result = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
     except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
         raise DataValidationError(f"Unable to read model results file: {path}") from exc
     if not isinstance(result, dict):
         raise DataValidationError(f"Invalid model results format: {path}")
     return result
 
 
 def load_model_performance_data(
     config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
 ) -> dict[str, Any]:
     """Load only saved training-CV metrics for baseline and tuned pipelines."""
     settings = validate_config(config if config is not None else load_config())
     paths = get_project_paths(settings)
     cv_results = _read_json(paths.reports_dir / "model_cv_results.json")
     tuning_results = _read_json(paths.tuning_results)
     if cv_results.get("holdout_evaluated") is not False:
         raise DataValidationError("Model CV report does not mark holdout unused")
     if tuning_results.get("holdout_used") is not False:
         raise DataValidationError("Tuning report indicates holdout use")
     if tuning_results.get("model_version") != settings["explainability"]["model_version"]:
         raise DataValidationError("Tuned results do not match configured model version")
     models = pd.DataFrame(cv_results.get("models", []))
     required = {
         "model",
         "balanced_accuracy_mean",
         "balanced_accuracy_std",
         "roc_auc_mean",
         "roc_auc_std",
         "recall_mean",
         "specificity_mean",
     }
     if models.empty or not required.issubset(models.columns):
         raise DataValidationError("Saved CV results lack required performance metrics")
     return {
         "candidate_cv": models,
         "tuning": tuning_results,
         "model_name": tuning_results["selected_model"],
         "model_version": tuning_results["model_version"],

 ) -> dict[str, Any]:

         "groups": groups,
         "local": local,
         "report": paths.explainability_report,
         "figure": paths.figures_dir / "fairness_group_rates.png",
     }

 def _input_value(
     column: str,
     default,
     allowed,
     *,
     numeric: bool,
     positive_numeric: bool = False,
 ):
     """Render a form field with an explicit optional-missing choice."""
     with st.container():
         not_provided = st.checkbox(
             "Not provided",
             key=f"missing_{column}",

         )

                 disabled=not_provided,
                 key=f"value_{column}",

         else:

                     index

 # Intelligent Loan Approval & Credit Risk Prediction System
 
 An academic decision-support prototype for exploring loan approval and credit
 risk prediction. It is not an autonomous lending decision engine.
 
 ## Current phase
 
 The project foundation, dataset profiling and quality audit, training-data
 EDA, leakage-safe preprocessing and feature engineering, model development,
 and Phase 5.1 evaluation are complete. Four candidate pipelines were compared
 by training-partition cross-validation; the selected model was then evaluated
 on the reserved holdout. Phase 5.2 tuning uses training-only stratified
 cross-validation and does not use holdout observations for search or comparison.
 
 ## Project layout
 
 ```text
 config.yaml             Central runtime configuration
 data/                   Raw, processed, and external data (private content ignored)
 notebooks/              Exploratory notebooks
 src/                    Configuration and domain-component packages
 app/                    Streamlit UI, pages, components, and services
 artifacts/               Generated model and report directories
 tests/                   Unit, integration, and validation tests
 docs/architecture.md    Architecture and responsibility boundaries
 logs/                   Local application logs (not committed)
 ```
 
 Configuration is loaded with `config.settings.load_config()`. The
 `loan_prediction.config` module remains as a compatibility import. Logging and
 random-seed helpers are in `utils/`.
 
 The root `config.yaml` owns dataset and artifact locations, split/CV settings,
 candidate model parameters, Streamlit page settings, and logging controls.
 `config.paths.ProjectPaths` resolves relative paths against the repository
 root, independent of the current working directory. Configuration validation
 fails with a `ConfigurationError` when required values are missing or invalid.
 Logs are emitted as structured JSON to the console and configured log file by
 default. Python and NumPy are seeded from `project.random_seed`; model
 estimators must use the same configured `project.random_seed` explicitly.
 
 ## Setup
 
 From the project root on Windows:
 
 ```powershell
 py -m venv env
 .\env\Scripts\Activate.ps1
 python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
 python -m pip install -e .
 ```
 
 ## Tests
 
 ```powershell
 python -m pytest
 ```
 
 ## Launch the Streamlit application
 
 ```powershell
 python -m streamlit run app.py
 ```
 
 The app includes a historical dashboard, an experimental prediction form,
 exploratory risk analysis, model-performance results, and project information.
 Historical dataset metrics and live browser-session predictions are kept
 separate. Predictions represent similarity to historical approval labels,
 not default or repayment risk.
 
 The UI palette is configured in `.streamlit/config.toml`; page styling and
 reusable UI components are in `app/components/`.
 
 ## Dependencies
 
 Runtime and test dependencies are version-pinned in `requirements.txt`; the
 project metadata and pytest configuration are in `pyproject.toml`.
 
 ## Data and modeling safeguards
 
 The labeled Kaggle loan data has been acquired and profiled separately from
 the unlabeled file. Candidate models use a stratified training/holdout split;
 all cross-validation fitting of imputation, encoding, scaling, and estimators
 occurs inside scikit-learn pipelines. Model selection used training-only CV
 balanced accuracy, with CV ROC-AUC as a tie-breaker, before the selected model
 was evaluated on the reserved holdout. No resampling is used; class weighting
 is applied within model fitting. The prediction application is intended to
 use a serialized pipeline fitted on training data.
 
 Dataset limitations, class balance, duplicate/overlapping records, evaluation
 metrics, and model limitations must be documented from observed data and
 measured results; none are assumed by this foundation.
 
 See [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) for package responsibilities,
 error handling, and planned application flow.
 
 The Kaggle source, acquisition details, and measured profiling summary are in
 [docs/dataset_source.md](docs/dataset_source.md). The detailed profile is
 saved as `artifacts/reports/dataset_profile.json`.
 
 The read-only data quality audit and interpretation are in
 `reports/data_quality_report.md`; raw CSVs are not modified by the audit.
 
 The training-data-only EDA notebook is
 [`notebooks/01_data_analysis.ipynb`](notebooks/01_data_analysis.ipynb). Run
 its cells top-to-bottom to regenerate `reports/figures/` and
 `reports/eda_report.md`. The notebook does not load the separate unlabeled
 Kaggle test CSV.
 
 The observed approval patterns, data limitations, feature considerations,
 preprocessing guidance, and potential demographic bias are discussed in
 [`reports/eda_insights.md`](reports/eda_insights.md). The report describes
 associations in the labeled sample and does not infer causation.
 
 The leakage-safe stratified split and fold-fitted transformation design are
 implemented in [`src/data/splitting.py`](src/data/splitting.py) and
 [`src/preprocessing/pipeline.py`](src/preprocessing/pipeline.py); usage and
 validation notes are in [`reports/preprocessing_report.md`](reports/preprocessing_report.md).
 
 Reusable income and loan feature engineering is implemented in
 [`src/features/engineering.py`](src/features/engineering.py) and runs inside
 the estimator pipeline. Its formulas, edge-case behavior, and test status are
 documented in [`reports/feature_engineering_report.md`](reports/feature_engineering_report.md).
 
 Model candidates and training workflow are implemented in
 [`src/models/classifiers.py`](src/models/classifiers.py) and
 [`src/models/train.py`](src/models/train.py). The executed workflow and its
 training-only cross-validation results are documented in
 [`reports/model_training_report.md`](reports/model_training_report.md). Run
 [`notebooks/03_model_training.ipynb`](notebooks/03_model_training.ipynb) to
 reproduce the training workflow; it does not evaluate the reserved holdout.
 
 Versioned complete pipelines are saved through the trusted local registry in
 [`src/models/registry.py`](src/models/registry.py). Loading requires registry

 """Interactive applicant form backed by the registered full ML pipeline."""

     get_form_defaults,
     load_prediction_model,
     predict_approval,
 )
 from config.settings import load_config
 from utils.exceptions import LoanPredictionError
 
 
 @st.cache_resource(show_spinner="Loading the registered model...")
 def _cached_model():
     return load_prediction_model()
 
 
 def _input_value(
     column: str,
     default,
     allowed,
     *,
     numeric: bool,
     positive_numeric: bool = False,
 ):
     """Render a form field with an explicit optional-missing choice."""
     with st.container():
         not_provided = st.checkbox(
             "Not provided",
             key=f"missing_{column}",
             help="The pipeline will handle this using its fitted training-fold imputer.",
         )
         if numeric:
             value = st.number_input(
                 column.replace("_", " "),
                 min_value=1.0 if positive_numeric else 0.0,
                 value=float(default),
                 step=100.0 if "Income" in column else 1.0,
                 disabled=not_provided,
                 key=f"value_{column}",
             )
         else:
             options = list(allowed)
             default_index = next(
                 (
                     index
                     for index, value in enumerate(options)
                     if value == default
                 ),
                 0,
             )
             value = st.selectbox(
                 column.replace("_", " "),
                 options=options,
                 index=default_index,
                 format_func=lambda item: (
                     "Good credit history" if column == "Credit_History" and item == 1
                     else "No credit history" if column == "Credit_History" and item == 0
                     else str(item)
                 ),
                 disabled=not_provided,
                 key=f"value_{column}",
             )
     return None if not_provided else value
 
 
 def render() -> None:
     """Render the model's historical approval-label estimate form."""
     render_page_header(
         "Decision-support prototype",
         "Loan Eligibility Predictor",
         "Explore how the registered model classifies one entered application "
         "against historical approval labels.",

     render_disclaimer(

         "not default probability, repayment likelihood, a credit score, or a "
         "lending decision. Review the inputs and use human oversight.",
     )
     config = load_config()
     try:
         defaults = get_form_defaults(config)
     except LoanPredictionError as exc:
         st.error(f"Prediction form could not load training-data examples: {exc}")
         return
 
     st.info(
         "Editable numeric defaults are medians and categorical defaults are "
         "modes from the labeled dataset. They are form examples, not recommended "
         "applicant values."
     )
     dataset_settings = config["dataset"]
     numeric_columns = dataset_settings["numeric_columns"]
     category_domains = dataset_settings["categorical_domains"]
     applicant: dict = {}
 
     with st.form("loan_prediction_form"):
         st.subheader("Applicant information")
         left, right = st.columns(2)
         with left:
             for column in numeric_columns[:2]:
                 applicant[column] = _input_value(
                     column,
                     defaults[column],
                     [],
                     numeric=True,
                     positive_numeric=(
                         column in dataset_settings["positive_numeric_columns"]
                     ),
                 )
             for column in list(category_domains)[:4]:
                 applicant[column] = _input_value(

                     defaults[column],
                     category_domains[column],
                     numeric=False,
                 )
         submitted = st.form_submit_button(

             type="primary",
             use_container_width=True,
         )
 
     if not submitted:
         return
     try:
         model, metadata = _cached_model()
         result = predict_approval(model, applicant, config)
     except LoanPredictionError as exc:
         st.error(f"Prediction could not be completed: {exc}")
         return

 """Local, one-feature-at-a-time sensitivity explanations for raw applicants."""
 
 from __future__ import annotations
 
 from pathlib import Path
 from typing import Any
 
 import matplotlib
 
 matplotlib.use("Agg")
 import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
 import numpy as np
 import pandas as pd
 
 from utils.exceptions import DataValidationError
 
 
 def _json_value(value: Any) -> Any:
     if pd.isna(value):
         return None
     if isinstance(value, np.generic):
         return value.item()
     return value
 
 
 def _reference_values(reference: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
     values: dict[str, Any] = {}
     for column in reference:
         series = reference[column]
         if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(series):
             values[column] = series.median()
         else:
             modes = series.mode(dropna=True)
             values[column] = modes.iloc[0] if not modes.empty else np.nan
     return pd.Series(values)
 
 
 def explain_local_prediction(
     model: Any,
     applicant: pd.DataFrame,
     reference: pd.DataFrame,
 ) -> dict[str, Any]:
     """Measure probability changes when each raw input is replaced by reference.
 
     This is a one-feature-at-a-time sensitivity check, not an additive
     attribution or a causal/counterfactual claim. Replacing correlated inputs
     independently can create unrealistic applicant profiles.
     """
     if len(applicant) != 1:
         raise DataValidationError("A local explanation requires exactly one row")
     if reference.empty or list(applicant.columns) != list(reference.columns):
         raise DataValidationError(
             "Local explanation reference must match the applicant feature schema"
         )
     if "Y" not in list(model.classes_):
         raise DataValidationError("Local explanation model has no approved class 'Y'")
 
     approved_index = list(model.classes_).index("Y")
     baseline_probability = float(
         model.predict_proba(applicant)[:, approved_index][0]
     )
     baseline_class = str(model.predict(applicant)[0])
     replacements = _reference_values(reference)
     sensitivities: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
     for feature in applicant.columns:
         changed = applicant.copy()
         if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(changed[feature]):
             changed[feature] = pd.to_numeric(changed[feature]).astype("float64")
         changed.loc[:, feature] = replacements[feature]
         probability = float(model.predict_proba(changed)[:, approved_index][0])
         sensitivities.append(
             {
                 "feature": feature,
                 "applicant_value": _json_value(applicant.iloc[0][feature]),
                 "reference_value": _json_value(replacements[feature]),
                 "approval_probability_after_replacement": probability,
                 "probability_delta": probability - baseline_probability,
             }
         )
     sensitivities.sort(
         key=lambda item: abs(item["probability_delta"]),
         reverse=True,
     )
     return {
         "baseline_approval_probability": baseline_probability,
         "predicted_class": baseline_class,
         "prediction_rule": "pipeline's default predict method",
         "reference_rows": int(len(reference)),
         "sensitivity_method": (
             "one original feature at a time replaced with reference median "
             "for numeric features or reference mode for categorical features"
         ),
         "interpretation_warning": (
             "Descriptive model sensitivity only; not causal, not additive, "
             "and not a lending rationale by itself."
         ),
         "features": sensitivities,
     }
 
 
 def save_local_explanation_chart(
     explanations: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
     output_path: Path,
 ) -> None:
     """Save local probability-change charts, with original feature labels."""
     if not explanations:
         raise DataValidationError("Cannot plot empty local explanations")
     figure, axes = plt.subplots(
         len(explanations),
         1,
         figsize=(10, max(4, 3.8 * len(explanations))),
         squeeze=False,
     )
     for axis, (case_name, explanation) in zip(axes[:, 0], explanations.items()):
         features = explanation["features"][:10]
         features = list(reversed(features))
         deltas = [row["probability_delta"] for row in features]
         labels = [row["feature"] for row in features]
         colors = ["#3c8d6d" if delta >= 0 else "#bd5a56" for delta in deltas]
         axis.barh(labels, deltas, color=colors)
         axis.axvline(0, color="black", linewidth=0.8)
         axis.set_title(
             f"{case_name}: baseline approval probability "
             f"{explanation['baseline_approval_probability']:.3f}"
         )
         axis.set_xlabel("Change in predicted approval probability")
         axis.set_ylabel("Original input feature")
     figure.tight_layout()
     figure.savefig(output_path, dpi=160, bbox_inches="tight")
     plt.close(figure)

 """Reproducible, class-imbalance-aware classifier factories."""
 
 from typing import Any
 
 from sklearn.base import BaseEstimator, ClassifierMixin
 from sklearn.ensemble import GradientBoostingClassifier, RandomForestClassifier
 from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
 from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier
 from sklearn.utils.class_weight import compute_sample_weight
 
 from config.settings import load_config, validate_config
 from utils.exceptions import ConfigurationError
 
 
 class BalancedGradientBoostingClassifier(ClassifierMixin, BaseEstimator):
     """Gradient boosting classifier with fold-local balanced sample weights."""
 
     def __init__(
         self,
         n_estimators: int = 100,
         learning_rate: float = 0.05,
         max_depth: int = 2,
         subsample: float = 1.0,
         random_state: int = 42,
     ) -> None:
         self.n_estimators = n_estimators
         self.learning_rate = learning_rate
         self.max_depth = max_depth
         self.subsample = subsample
         self.random_state = random_state
 
     def fit(self, X: Any, y: Any) -> "BalancedGradientBoostingClassifier":
         """Fit with weights computed solely from this fit call's target rows."""
         self.estimator_ = GradientBoostingClassifier(
             n_estimators=self.n_estimators,
             learning_rate=self.learning_rate,
             max_depth=self.max_depth,
             subsample=self.subsample,
             random_state=self.random_state,
         )
         sample_weight = compute_sample_weight(class_weight="balanced", y=y)
         self.estimator_.fit(X, y, sample_weight=sample_weight)
         self.classes_ = self.estimator_.classes_
         self.n_features_in_ = self.estimator_.n_features_in_
         if hasattr(self.estimator_, "feature_names_in_"):
             self.feature_names_in_ = self.estimator_.feature_names_in_
         return self
 
     def predict(self, X: Any) -> Any:
         """Predict labels with the fitted gradient boosting model."""
         return self.estimator_.predict(X)
 
     def predict_proba(self, X: Any) -> Any:
         """Return fitted gradient boosting class probabilities."""
         return self.estimator_.predict_proba(X)
 
 
 def build_classifiers(
     config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
 ) -> dict[str, BaseEstimator]:
     """Construct configured classifier candidates with a shared seed."""
     settings = validate_config(config if config is not None else load_config())
     seed = settings["project"]["random_seed"]
     parameters = settings["models"]["parameters"]
     candidates = settings["models"]["candidates"]
     factories: dict[str, BaseEstimator] = {
         "logistic_regression": LogisticRegression(
             max_iter=parameters["logistic_regression"]["max_iter"],
             solver=parameters["logistic_regression"]["solver"],
             class_weight=parameters["logistic_regression"]["class_weight"],
             random_state=seed,
         ),
         "decision_tree": DecisionTreeClassifier(
             max_depth=parameters["decision_tree"]["max_depth"],
             min_samples_leaf=parameters["decision_tree"]["min_samples_leaf"],
             class_weight=parameters["decision_tree"]["class_weight"],
             random_state=seed,
         ),
         "random_forest": RandomForestClassifier(
             n_estimators=parameters["random_forest"]["n_estimators"],
             max_features=parameters["random_forest"]["max_features"],
             min_samples_leaf=parameters["random_forest"]["min_samples_leaf"],
             class_weight=parameters["random_forest"]["class_weight"],
             n_jobs=parameters["random_forest"]["n_jobs"],
             random_state=seed,
         ),
         "gradient_boosting": BalancedGradientBoostingClassifier(
             n_estimators=parameters["gradient_boosting"]["n_estimators"],
             learning_rate=parameters["gradient_boosting"]["learning_rate"],
             max_depth=parameters["gradient_boosting"]["max_depth"],
             subsample=parameters["gradient_boosting"]["subsample"],
             random_state=seed,
         ),
     }
     unknown_candidates = sorted(set(candidates).difference(factories))
     if unknown_candidates:
         raise ConfigurationError(
             f"Unsupported configured model candidates: {unknown_candidates}"
         )
     return {name: factories[name] for name in candidates}

 @dataclass(frozen=True)

     """Model features and target in independent training and holdout sets."""

 def get_model_feature_columns(config: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
     """Return the configured, prediction-time feature allowlist."""

     dataset = settings["dataset"]
     numeric_columns = tuple(dataset["numeric_columns"])
     categorical_columns = tuple(dataset["categorical_domains"])
     feature_columns = (*numeric_columns, *categorical_columns)
 
     if len(feature_columns) != len(set(feature_columns)):
         raise DataValidationError(
             "Configured numeric and categorical feature columns must be distinct"
         )
     excluded = set(dataset["identifier_columns"]).union(
         {dataset["target_column"]}

             "Configured model features must not include target or identifier columns"

     frame: pd.DataFrame,

     random_state: int | None = None,

 ) -> DataSplit:
     """Validate and stratify labeled rows before fitting any transformations.
 
     The configured feature allowlist excludes the target, identifiers, and any
     other columns not explicitly declared as prediction-time inputs. Exact
     duplicate feature rows are rejected rather than allowed to cross
     partitions. The returned holdout is reserved for final evaluation.
     """
     settings = validate_config(config if config is not None else load_config())
     dataset_settings = settings["dataset"]
     training_settings = settings["training"]
     target_column = dataset_settings["target_column"]
     identifiers = tuple(dataset_settings["identifier_columns"])
 
     validate_labeled_dataset(
         frame,
         target_column=target_column,
         allowed_target_values=dataset_settings["target_classes"],
         identifier_columns=identifiers,
     )
 
     feature_columns = get_model_feature_columns(settings)
     missing_features = [name for name in feature_columns if name not in frame.columns]
     if missing_features:
         raise DataValidationError(
             f"Labeled dataset is missing configured model features: {missing_features}"
         )
 
     X = frame.loc[:, feature_columns].copy()
     y = frame.loc[:, target_column].copy()
     if X.duplicated(keep=False).any():
         raise DataValidationError(
             "Duplicate model-feature rows found; resolve duplicate or conflicting "
             "records before splitting to prevent partition leakage"
         )
 
     split_size = (
         training_settings["test_size"] if test_size is None else test_size
     )
     seed = settings["project"]["random_seed"] if random_state is None else random_state
     if isinstance(split_size, bool) or not isinstance(split_size, (int, float)):
         raise DataValidationError("test_size must be a number between 0 and 1")

     if isinstance(seed, bool) or not isinstance(seed, int):
         raise DataValidationError("random_state must be an integer")

         X_test=X_test,

         y_test=y_test,

 from typing import Any

 def build_preprocessor(config: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> ColumnTransformer:
     """Build an unfitted transformer for the configured model feature schema.
 
     Fitting this transformer must happen only on training data. When used in
     cross-validation, pass it inside an estimator pipeline so each fold fits
     its own imputers, scaler, and encoder.
     """
     settings = validate_config(config if config is not None else load_config())
     dataset = settings["dataset"]
     numeric_columns = list(dataset["numeric_columns"])
     engineered_numeric_columns = [
         "Total_Income",
         "Loan_to_Income_Ratio",
         *(
             f"{column}_log1p"
             for column in settings["feature_engineering"]["log1p_columns"]
         ),
     ]
     categorical_columns = list(dataset["categorical_domains"])
     feature_columns = get_model_feature_columns(settings)
     if not numeric_columns or not categorical_columns:
         raise DataValidationError(
             "Preprocessing requires configured numeric and categorical features"
         )
     if len(feature_columns) != len(numeric_columns) + len(categorical_columns):
         raise DataValidationError(
             "Numeric and categorical preprocessing columns must be distinct"
         )
     numeric_columns.extend(engineered_numeric_columns)
 
     return ColumnTransformer(
         transformers=[
             ("numeric", make_numeric_pipeline(), numeric_columns),
             ("categorical", make_categorical_pipeline(), categorical_columns),
         ],
         remainder="drop",
         verbose_feature_names_out=False,
     )

     estimator: BaseEstimator,
     config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
 ) -> Pipeline:
     """Place an estimator after preprocessing for fold-local fitting.
 
     Use this complete pipeline with cross-validation or hyperparameter search;
     do not preprocess the full dataset before passing data to those routines.
     """
     if estimator is None:
         raise DataValidationError("An estimator is required to build the pipeline")
     settings = validate_config(config if config is not None else load_config())
     return Pipeline(
         steps=[
             (
                 "feature_engineering",
                 LoanFeatureEngineer(
                     numeric_columns=settings["dataset"]["numeric_columns"],
                     log1p_columns=settings["feature_engineering"]["log1p_columns"],
                     excluded_columns=(
                         *settings["dataset"]["identifier_columns"],
                         settings["dataset"]["target_column"],
                     ),
                 ),
             ),
             ("preprocessor", build_preprocessor(config)),
             ("estimator", estimator),

     )

 """Deterministic loan-applicant feature engineering."""
 
 from collections.abc import Sequence
 
 import numpy as np
 import pandas as pd
 from sklearn.base import BaseEstimator, TransformerMixin
 from sklearn.utils.validation import check_is_fitted
 
 from utils.exceptions import DataValidationError
 
 
 class LoanFeatureEngineer(BaseEstimator, TransformerMixin):
     """Create income/loan features without learning from rows or target values.
 
     Missing, non-numeric, and non-finite numeric inputs are represented as
     ``NaN`` for downstream training-fold imputation. Ratios with nonpositive
     total income and log1p values outside the nonnegative domain are ``NaN``.
     Finite extreme values are not clipped using arbitrary or holdout-derived
     limits; non-finite results from arithmetic are converted to ``NaN``.
     """
 
     def __init__(
         self,
         numeric_columns: Sequence[str] = (
             "ApplicantIncome",
             "CoapplicantIncome",
             "LoanAmount",
             "Loan_Amount_Term",
         ),
         log1p_columns: Sequence[str] = (),
         excluded_columns: Sequence[str] = (),
     ) -> None:
         self.numeric_columns = numeric_columns
         self.log1p_columns = log1p_columns
         self.excluded_columns = excluded_columns
 
     def fit(
         self,
         X: pd.DataFrame,
         y: pd.Series | None = None,
     ) -> "LoanFeatureEngineer":
         """Validate required inputs without estimating any data statistics."""
         del y
         if not isinstance(X, pd.DataFrame):
             raise DataValidationError("Feature engineering input must be a DataFrame")
         required_columns = set(self.numeric_columns).union(
             {"ApplicantIncome", "CoapplicantIncome", "LoanAmount"}
         )
         missing_columns = sorted(required_columns.difference(X.columns))
         if missing_columns:
             raise DataValidationError(
                 f"Feature engineering input is missing required columns: "
                 f"{missing_columns}"
             )
         valid_log_columns = set(X.columns).union({"Total_Income"})
         invalid_log_columns = sorted(set(self.log1p_columns).difference(valid_log_columns))
         if invalid_log_columns:
             raise DataValidationError(
                 f"Cannot apply log1p to unconfigured feature columns: "
                 f"{invalid_log_columns}"
             )
         input_columns = X.drop(columns=list(self.excluded_columns), errors="ignore")
         self.feature_names_in_ = np.asarray(input_columns.columns, dtype=object)
         self.n_features_in_ = len(input_columns.columns)
         return self
 
     @staticmethod
     def _finite_numeric(series: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
         numeric = pd.to_numeric(series, errors="coerce").astype("float64")
         return numeric.where(np.isfinite(numeric), np.nan)
 
     def transform(self, X: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
         """Return sanitized inputs plus derived numeric features."""
         check_is_fitted(self, attributes=["feature_names_in_"])
         if not isinstance(X, pd.DataFrame):
             raise DataValidationError("Feature engineering input must be a DataFrame")
         transformed = X.drop(
             columns=list(self.excluded_columns),
             errors="ignore",
         ).copy()
         missing_columns = sorted(
             set(self.feature_names_in_).difference(transformed.columns)
         )
         if missing_columns:
             raise DataValidationError(
                 f"Feature engineering input is missing fitted columns: "
                 f"{missing_columns}"
             )
 
         for column in self.numeric_columns:
             transformed[column] = self._finite_numeric(transformed[column])
 
         with np.errstate(over="ignore", invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
             total_income = (
                 transformed["ApplicantIncome"] + transformed["CoapplicantIncome"]
             )
             total_income = total_income.where(np.isfinite(total_income), np.nan)
             transformed["Total_Income"] = total_income
 
             valid_ratio = (
                 transformed["Total_Income"].gt(0)
                 & transformed["LoanAmount"].ge(0)
             )
             ratio = transformed["LoanAmount"].div(
                 transformed["Total_Income"].where(valid_ratio)
             )
             transformed["Loan_to_Income_Ratio"] = ratio.where(
                 valid_ratio & np.isfinite(ratio), np.nan
             )
 
             for column in self.log1p_columns:
                 values = (
                     transformed["Total_Income"]
                     if column == "Total_Income"
                     else self._finite_numeric(transformed[column])
                 )
                 valid_log = values.ge(0)
                 logged = np.log1p(values.where(valid_log))
                 transformed[f"{column}_log1p"] = logged.where(
                     valid_log & np.isfinite(logged), np.nan
                 )
 
         return transformed.drop(
             columns=list(self.excluded_columns),
             errors="ignore",
         )
 
     def get_feature_names_out(
         self,
         input_features: Sequence[str] | None = None,
     ) -> np.ndarray:
         """Return names emitted by the transformation."""
         check_is_fitted(self, attributes=["feature_names_in_"])
         names = (
             list(input_features)
             if input_features is not None
             else list(self.feature_names_in_)
         )
         names.extend(["Total_Income", "Loan_to_Income_Ratio"])
         names.extend(f"{column}_log1p" for column in self.log1p_columns)
         return np.asarray(
             [name for name in names if name not in self.excluded_columns],
             dtype=object,
         )

 import streamlit as st
 
 from app.components.theme import render_disclaimer, render_page_header
 from app.services.dashboard_service import load_explainability_data
 from utils.exceptions import LoanPredictionError
 
 
 def render() -> None:

     render_page_header(

         "Rates on this page refer to historical approval labels and "

     )
     try:
         outputs = load_explainability_data()
     except LoanPredictionError as exc:
         st.error(f"Risk analysis outputs could not be loaded: {exc}")
         return
 
     groups = outputs["groups"]
     st.subheader("Out-of-fold subgroup metrics")
     st.caption(
         "Training-partition folds only. Small groups have unstable rates; "
         "descriptive differences do not prove fairness or discrimination."
     )
     st.dataframe(
         groups.rename(
             columns={
                 "attribute": "Attribute",
                 "group": "Group",
                 "n": "Applications",
                 "eligible_for_comparison": "Meets minimum group size",
                 "approval_rate": "Model approval rate",
                 "observed_approval_rate": "Historical approval rate",
                 "true_positive_rate": "Recall for historical approvals",
                 "false_positive_rate": "False positive rate for historical rejections",
             }
         ).style.format(
             {
                 "Model approval rate": "{:.1%}",
                 "Historical approval rate": "{:.1%}",
                 "Recall for historical approvals": "{:.1%}",
                 "False positive rate for historical rejections": "{:.1%}",
             },
             na_rep="Not estimable",
         ),
         use_container_width=True,
         hide_index=True,
     )
     st.image(
         str(outputs["figure"]),
         caption="Out-of-fold group rates; these are not default or loss rates.",
         use_container_width=True,
     )
 
     st.subheader("Global predictive feature importance")
     st.caption(
         "Permutation importance measures changes in CV balanced accuracy "
         "when one original feature is shuffled. It is not causal influence."
     )
     st.dataframe(
         outputs["importance"].rename(
             columns={
                 "feature": "Original input feature",
                 "importance_mean": "Mean CV score decrease",
                 "importance_fold_std": "Fold standard deviation",
                 "importance_repeat_std": "Permutation-repeat standard deviation",
             }
         ).style.format(
             {
                 "Mean CV score decrease": "{:.4f}",
                 "Fold standard deviation": "{:.4f}",
                 "Permutation-repeat standard deviation": "{:.4f}",
             }
         ),
         use_container_width=True,
         hide_index=True,
     )
     local = outputs["local"]
     with st.expander("Illustrative individual model sensitivities"):
         for case_name, explanation in local.items():
             st.markdown(
                 f"**{case_name.replace('_', ' ').title()}** — "
                 f"predicted `{explanation['predicted_class']}`, approval "
                 f"probability {explanation['baseline_approval_probability']:.1%}."
             )
             st.dataframe(
                 [
                     {
                         "Feature": item["feature"],
                         "Entered value": item["applicant_value"],
                         "Reference value": item["reference_value"],
                         "Probability change": item["probability_delta"],
                     }
                     for item in explanation["features"][:5]
                 ],
                 hide_index=True,
                 use_container_width=True,
             )
             st.caption(explanation["interpretation_warning"])
 
     render_disclaimer(
         "Subgroup gaps may reflect sample size, missingness, historic policy, "
         "label quality, or other factors. This analysis is not a legal fairness "
         "assessment and is not sufficient for credit decisions."
     )

 """Read-only services for dashboard statistics and model results."""
 
 import json
 from pathlib import Path
 from typing import Any
 
 import pandas as pd
 
 from config.paths import get_project_paths
 from config.settings import load_config, validate_config
 from data.loader import load_csv
 from utils.exceptions import DataValidationError
 
 
 def load_historical_dashboard_data(
     config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
 ) -> dict[str, Any]:
     """Calculate historical application counts and observed label breakdowns."""
     settings = validate_config(config if config is not None else load_config())
     paths = get_project_paths(settings)
     frame = load_csv(paths.labeled_dataset)
     target_column = settings["dataset"]["target_column"]
     target_classes = settings["dataset"]["target_classes"]
     if target_column not in frame or frame[target_column].isna().any():
         raise DataValidationError("Historical dashboard target is missing or invalid")
 
     counts = frame[target_column].value_counts().reindex(target_classes, fill_value=0)
     if int(counts.sum()) != len(frame) or (counts <= 0).any():
         raise DataValidationError("Historical target counts do not match dataset rows")
     approval_count = int(counts["Y"])
     rejection_count = int(counts["N"])
     approval_by_area = (
         frame.groupby(["Property_Area", target_column], observed=False)
         .size()
         .unstack(fill_value=0)
         .reindex(columns=target_classes, fill_value=0)
         .rename(columns={"Y": "Y", "N": "N"})
         .rename_axis("Property_Area")
         .reset_index()
     )
     return {
         "application_count": int(len(frame)),
         "approval_count": approval_count,
         "rejection_count": rejection_count,
         "approval_rate": approval_count / len(frame),
         "rejection_rate": rejection_count / len(frame),
         "status_counts": counts.rename(index={"Y": "Approved", "N": "Rejected"}),
         "approval_by_area": approval_by_area,
         "source": str(paths.labeled_dataset),
         "target_column": target_column,
     }
 
 
 def _read_json(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
     try:
         result = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
     except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
         raise DataValidationError(f"Unable to read model results file: {path}") from exc
     if not isinstance(result, dict):
         raise DataValidationError(f"Invalid model results format: {path}")
     return result
 
 
 def load_model_performance_data(
     config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
 ) -> dict[str, Any]:
     """Load only saved training-CV metrics for baseline and tuned pipelines."""
     settings = validate_config(config if config is not None else load_config())
     paths = get_project_paths(settings)
     cv_results = _read_json(paths.cv_results)
     tuning_results = _read_json(paths.tuning_results)
     if cv_results.get("holdout_evaluated") is not False:
         raise DataValidationError("Model CV report does not mark holdout unused")
     if tuning_results.get("holdout_used") is not False:
         raise DataValidationError("Tuning report indicates holdout use")
     if tuning_results.get("model_version") != settings["explainability"]["model_version"]:
         raise DataValidationError("Tuned results do not match configured model version")
     models = pd.DataFrame(cv_results.get("models", []))
     required = {
         "model",
         "balanced_accuracy_mean",
         "balanced_accuracy_std",
         "roc_auc_mean",
         "roc_auc_std",
         "recall_mean",
         "specificity_mean",
     }
     if models.empty or not required.issubset(models.columns):
         raise DataValidationError("Saved CV results lack required performance metrics")
     return {
         "candidate_cv": models,
         "tuning": tuning_results,
         "model_name": tuning_results["selected_model"],
         "model_version": tuning_results["model_version"],
         "cv_folds": tuning_results["cv_folds"],
         "training_rows": tuning_results["training_rows"],
     }
 
 
 def load_explainability_data(
     config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
 ) -> dict[str, Any]:
     """Read the Phase 6.1 explanation reports for the risk analysis page."""
     settings = validate_config(config if config is not None else load_config())
     paths = get_project_paths(settings)
     try:
         importance = pd.read_csv(paths.global_importance)
         groups = pd.read_csv(paths.fairness_results)
         local = _read_json(paths.local_explanations)
     except (OSError, pd.errors.EmptyDataError, pd.errors.ParserError) as exc:
         raise DataValidationError("Unable to read explainability outputs") from exc
     if importance.empty or groups.empty or not local:
         raise DataValidationError("Explainability outputs are incomplete")
     return {
         "importance": importance,
         "groups": groups,
         "local": local,
         "report": paths.explainability_report,
         "figure": paths.figures_dir / "fairness_group_rates.png",
     }

 # Phase 5.1 — Model evaluation
 
 ## Protocol
 
 - Positive class: `Y` (approved); negative class: `N` (rejected).
 - Selection used training-partition CV only: highest mean stratified CV balanced accuracy, with mean ROC-AUC as the tie-breaker.
 - Selected candidate: `random_forest` version `1.0.0`.
 - Selection scores: balanced accuracy 0.684495; ROC-AUC 0.778701.
 - The final stratified holdout was evaluated after selection (123 rows); it was not used for preprocessing, CV, selection, or threshold tuning.
 - Fitted class ordering: `['N', 'Y']`; probability column 1 was used for positive class `Y`.
 - Undefined precision/recall/F1 use `zero_division=0`; ROC-AUC is reported as unavailable if the holdout contains only one class; specificity is unavailable if no negatives are present.
 - Independent confusion-matrix calculations were compared against the metric-library results.
 
 ## Cross-validation comparison
 
 Values are mean ± standard deviation across identical stratified training folds; standard deviation summarizes fold variation. The holdout is not included in this comparison.
 
 | Model | Accuracy | Balanced accuracy | ROC-AUC | Specificity | Precision (Y) | Recall (Y) | F1 (Y) |

 # Phase 6.1 — Explainable AI and exploratory fairness review
 
 ## Scope and method
 
 - Model: `random_forest` version `1.1.0`.
 - Explanations use only the 491-row training partition. The 123-row holdout was not passed to these analyses.
 - Global importance is permutation importance over original input columns, measured on each stratified CV validation fold. The complete pipeline regenerates engineered and one-hot encoded features after each raw input column is permuted.
 - Local cases use out-of-fold predictions. For each, the model fitted without that case's fold is used for one-feature-at-a-time sensitivity replacements against that fold's training-data medians/modes.
 - Fairness metrics use the same out-of-fold class predictions and report observed approval rates alongside model selection and error rates.
 - The optimized model's prior training/holdout split is respected here. The holdout had been evaluated for the baseline model during Phase 5.1; that historical exposure is not reversed by this analysis.
 
 ## Global permutation importance
 
 | Original feature | Mean balanced-accuracy decrease | SD across folds |
 |---|---:|---:|
 | `Credit_History` | 0.1823 | 0.0670 |
 | `ApplicantIncome` | 0.0346 | 0.0346 |
 | `LoanAmount` | 0.0342 | 0.0319 |
 | `CoapplicantIncome` | 0.0309 | 0.0287 |
 | `Education` | 0.0067 | 0.0066 |
 | `Property_Area` | 0.0051 | 0.0075 |
 | `Gender` | 0.0014 | 0.0082 |
 | `Self_Employed` | 0.0012 | 0.0019 |
 | `Married` | 0.0002 | 0.0117 |
 | `Dependents` | -0.0012 | 0.0102 |
 
 Negative permutation importance can occur when shuffling improves a fold score; correlated inputs can share or mask importance. Derived-feature effects are reflected through their original input columns rather than ranked as separate, independently permutable fields.
 
 ![Cross-validated permutation importance](figures/global_permutation_importance.png)
 
 ## Local prediction sensitivity
 
 Each example changes one raw input at a time to the training-fold reference median (numeric) or mode (categorical) and measures the resulting change in approval probability. This is not additive attribution. Independent replacements can create implausible combinations, and these changes are not causal explanations.
 
 ### Lower Out Of Fold Approval Probability
 
 - Predicted class: `N`.
 - Out-of-fold approval probability: 0.0021.
 - Largest one-at-a-time probability sensitivities:
 
 | Feature | Applicant value | Reference value | Probability change |
 |---|---|---|---:|
 | `Credit_History` | `0.0` | `1.0` | +0.8910 |
 | `Property_Area` | `Rural` | `Semiurban` | +0.0344 |
 | `Dependents` | `3+` | `0` | -0.0021 |
 | `ApplicantIncome` | `3400` | `3859.0` | +0.0017 |
 | `CoapplicantIncome` | `2500.0` | `1086.0` | +0.0000 |
 
 ### Higher Out Of Fold Approval Probability
 
 - Predicted class: `Y`.
 - Out-of-fold approval probability: 0.9963.
 - Largest one-at-a-time probability sensitivities:
 
 | Feature | Applicant value | Reference value | Probability change |
 |---|---|---|---:|
 | `CoapplicantIncome` | `2417.0` | `1126.0` | -0.3876 |
 | `ApplicantIncome` | `2333` | `3775.0` | -0.2119 |
 | `LoanAmount` | `136.0` | `128.0` | -0.0080 |
 | `Property_Area` | `Urban` | `Semiurban` | +0.0014 |
 | `Loan_Amount_Term` | `360.0` | `360.0` | +0.0000 |
 
 ![Local prediction sensitivities](figures/local_prediction_sensitivities.png)
 
 ## Exploratory subgroup review
 
 The reviewed attributes are `Gender`, `Education`, `Married`, as available in the source data. These are limited observed attributes, not a complete demographic or legal fairness audit.
 
 | Attribute | Eligible groups | Approval-rate range | TPR range | FPR range | Min/max approval-rate ratio |
 |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
 | `Gender` | 3 | 0.1575 | 0.0609 | 0.2903 | 0.8016 |
 | `Education` | 2 | 0.0665 | 0.0010 | 0.0844 | 0.9174 |
 | `Married` | 2 | 0.0151 | 0.0029 | 0.1213 | 0.9811 |
 
 Group sizes and the underlying selection, observed approval, TPR, and FPR rates are in `artifacts/reports/fairness_group_metrics.csv`. Groups below the configured minimum are retained in the data but excluded from range comparisons. Missing subgroup membership is shown explicitly.
 
 | Attribute | Group | n | Model approval | Observed approval | TPR | FPR |
 |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
 | `Gender` | `Male` | 393 | 0.7939 | 0.6845 | 0.9108 | 0.5403 |
 | `Gender` | `Female` | 87 | 0.7931 | 0.7011 | 0.9180 | 0.5000 |
 | `Gender` | `Missing` | 11 | 0.6364 | 0.6364 | 0.8571 | 0.2500 |
 | `Education` | `Graduate` | 380 | 0.8053 | 0.7079 | 0.9108 | 0.5495 |
 | `Education` | `Not Graduate` | 111 | 0.7387 | 0.6126 | 0.9118 | 0.4651 |
 | `Married` | `No` | 169 | 0.7988 | 0.6450 | 0.9083 | 0.6000 |
 | `Married` | `Yes` | 319 | 0.7837 | 0.7053 | 0.9111 | 0.4787 |
 | `Married` | `Missing` | 3 | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | not estimable |
 
 ![Exploratory subgroup rates](figures/fairness_group_rates.png)
 
 Differences are descriptive and may reflect sampling variation, historical decisions, label quality, or other omitted factors. They do not establish discrimination or its absence, satisfy a legal standard, or support causal claims. The dataset has only 491 training rows and lacks important demographic and socioeconomic context, so small-group rates are especially uncertain.
 
 ## SHAP
 
 SHAP was not run because the optional `shap` package is not installed in the current environment. No SHAP values were fabricated. The implemented SHAP path accepts original named features through the complete pipeline when the package is installed and compatible.
 
 ## Decision-support limitation
 
 These explanations describe model behavior, not applicant worthiness. No explanation, feature-importance ranking, or subgroup metric should be presented as the sole reason for a lending decision. Human review, appropriate validation, and domain/legal assessment remain necessary.

 from __future__ import annotations

 from utils.exceptions import ArtifactError, DataValidationError
 
 POSITIVE_LABEL = "Y"
 NEGATIVE_LABEL = "N"
 SELECTION_METRIC = "balanced_accuracy_mean"
 
 
 @dataclass(frozen=True)
 class EvaluationResult:
     """Selected candidate's holdout scores, CV comparison, and outputs."""
 
     selected_model: str

 def select_model_from_cv(
     cv_results: pd.DataFrame,
     model_names: list[str] | None = None,
 ) -> str:
     """Select by mean CV balanced accuracy, then mean CV ROC-AUC.
 
     The selector accepts CV results only. It has no holdout parameter or
     access to holdout labels/predictions.
     """
     required = {"model", "balanced_accuracy_mean", "roc_auc_mean"}
     missing_columns = required.difference(cv_results.columns)
     if missing_columns:
         raise DataValidationError(
             f"CV results are missing selection columns: {sorted(missing_columns)}"
         )
     candidates = cv_results.copy()
     if model_names is not None:
         candidates = candidates[candidates["model"].isin(model_names)]
     if candidates.empty:
         raise DataValidationError("No CV model candidates are available")
     scores = candidates[["balanced_accuracy_mean", "roc_auc_mean"]].to_numpy(
         dtype=float
     )
     if not np.isfinite(scores).all():
         raise DataValidationError("CV selection metrics must be finite")
     candidates = candidates.sort_values(
         ["balanced_accuracy_mean", "roc_auc_mean", "model"],
         ascending=[False, False, True],
         kind="mergesort",
     )
     return str(candidates.iloc[0]["model"])
 
 
 def _read_cv_results(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
     try:
         payload = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
     except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
         raise DataValidationError(f"Unable to read CV results: {path}") from exc
     if not isinstance(payload, dict) or not isinstance(payload.get("models"), list):
         raise DataValidationError(f"Invalid CV results format: {path}")
     return payload
 
 
 def _positive_probability(model: Any, X: pd.DataFrame) -> np.ndarray:
     classes = getattr(model, "classes_", None)
     if classes is None:
         raise ArtifactError("Selected model does not expose fitted class ordering")
     class_labels = list(classes)
     if POSITIVE_LABEL not in class_labels:
         raise ArtifactError(
             f"Selected model has no positive class {POSITIVE_LABEL!r}: {class_labels}"
         )
     probabilities = model.predict_proba(X)
     if probabilities.ndim != 2 or probabilities.shape[1] != len(class_labels):
         raise ArtifactError("Model probability output does not match class ordering")
     positive_index = class_labels.index(POSITIVE_LABEL)
     return np.asarray(probabilities[:, positive_index], dtype=float)
 
 
 def _calculate_metrics(
     y_true: pd.Series,
     y_pred: np.ndarray,
     positive_probabilities: np.ndarray,
 ) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], np.ndarray]:
     labels = [NEGATIVE_LABEL, POSITIVE_LABEL]
     matrix = confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred, labels=labels)
     tn, fp, fn, tp = (int(value) for value in matrix.ravel())
     specificity_denominator = tn + fp
     specificity = (
         float(tn / specificity_denominator)
         if specificity_denominator
         else None
     )
     class_recall_values = [
         true_positive / actual_count
         for true_positive, actual_count in (
             (tn, tn + fp),
             (tp, tp + fn),
         )
         if actual_count
     ]
     positive_present = bool((y_true == POSITIVE_LABEL).any())
     negative_present = bool((y_true == NEGATIVE_LABEL).any())
     roc_auc: float | None = None
     if positive_present and negative_present:
         roc_auc = float(
             roc_auc_score(
                 (y_true == POSITIVE_LABEL).astype(int),
                 positive_probabilities,
             )
         )
         positive_count = int((y_true == POSITIVE_LABEL).sum())
         negative_count = int((y_true == NEGATIVE_LABEL).sum())
         ranks = pd.Series(positive_probabilities).rank(method="average").to_numpy()
         positive_rank_sum = float(
             ranks[(y_true.to_numpy() == POSITIVE_LABEL)].sum()
         )
         independent_roc_auc = (
             positive_rank_sum - positive_count * (positive_count + 1) / 2
         ) / (positive_count * negative_count)
         if not np.isclose(roc_auc, independent_roc_auc, rtol=0.0, atol=1e-12):
             raise AssertionError("Independent ROC-AUC verification disagreed")
 
     metrics: dict[str, Any] = {
         "accuracy": float(accuracy_score(y_true, y_pred)),
         "precision": float(
             precision_score(
                 y_true,
                 y_pred,
                 pos_label=POSITIVE_LABEL,
                 zero_division=0,
             )
         ),
         "recall": float(
             recall_score(
                 y_true,
                 y_pred,
                 pos_label=POSITIVE_LABEL,
                 zero_division=0,
             )
         ),
         "f1": float(
             f1_score(
                 y_true,
                 y_pred,
                 pos_label=POSITIVE_LABEL,
                 zero_division=0,
             )
         ),
         "roc_auc": roc_auc,
         "specificity": specificity,
         "balanced_accuracy": float(np.mean(class_recall_values)),
         "confusion_matrix": {
             "labels": labels,
             "tn": tn,
             "fp": fp,
             "fn": fn,
             "tp": tp,
         },
         "positive_class": POSITIVE_LABEL,
         "negative_class": NEGATIVE_LABEL,
         "positive_probability_column_index": None,
     }
 
     independently_calculated = {
         "accuracy": (tn + tp) / (tn + fp + fn + tp),
         "precision": tp / (tp + fp) if tp + fp else 0.0,
         "recall": tp / (tp + fn) if tp + fn else 0.0,
         "specificity": tn / (tn + fp) if tn + fp else None,
         "balanced_accuracy": (
             (
                 (tp / (tp + fn) if tp + fn else 0.0)
                 + (tn / (tn + fp) if tn + fp else 0.0)
             )
             / (int(bool(tp + fn)) + int(bool(tn + fp)))
         ),
     }
     for metric, independent_value in independently_calculated.items():
         measured = metrics[metric]
         if independent_value is None:
             if measured is not None:
                 raise AssertionError(f"Independent {metric} verification disagreed")

 # Intelligent Loan Approval & Credit Risk Prediction System
 
 An academic decision-support prototype for exploring loan approval and credit
 risk prediction. It is not an autonomous lending decision engine.
 
 ## Current phase
 
 Phases 0 through 7.2 are complete. The Streamlit predictor uses the registered
 v1.1.0 pipeline and configured 11-column applicant schema. It validates
 inputs, supports optional missing values, and provides class-only local
 sensitivity checks. Probability output remains disabled because calibration
 has not been validated.
 
 ## Project layout
 
 ```text
 config.yaml             Central runtime configuration
 data/                   Raw, processed, and external data (private content ignored)
 notebooks/              Exploratory notebooks
 src/                    Configuration and domain-component packages
 app/                    Streamlit UI, pages, components, and services
 artifacts/               Generated model and report directories
 tests/                   Unit, integration, and validation tests
 docs/architecture.md    Architecture and responsibility boundaries
 logs/                   Local application logs (not committed)
 ```
 
 Configuration is loaded with `config.settings.load_config()`. The
 `loan_prediction.config` module remains as a compatibility import. Logging and
 random-seed helpers are in `utils/`.
 
 The root `config.yaml` owns dataset and artifact locations, split/CV settings,
 candidate model parameters, Streamlit page settings, and logging controls.
 `config.paths.ProjectPaths` resolves relative paths against the repository
 root, independent of the current working directory. Configuration validation
 fails with a `ConfigurationError` when required values are missing or invalid.
 Logs are emitted as structured JSON to the console and configured log file by
 default. Python and NumPy are seeded from `project.random_seed`; model
 estimators must use the same configured `project.random_seed` explicitly.
 
 ## Setup
 
 From the project root on Windows:
 
 ```powershell
 py -m venv env
 .\env\Scripts\Activate.ps1
 python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
 python -m pip install -e .
 ```
 
 ## Tests
 
 ```powershell
 python -m pytest
 ```
 
 ## Launch the Streamlit application
 
 ```powershell
 python -m streamlit run app.py
 ```
 
 The app includes a historical dashboard, an experimental prediction form,
 exploratory risk analysis, model-performance results, and project information.
 Historical dataset metrics and live browser-session predictions are kept
 separate. Predictions represent similarity to historical approval labels,
 not default or repayment risk.
 
 The UI palette is configured in `.streamlit/config.toml`; page styling and
 reusable UI components are in `app/components/`.
 
 The current UI screenshots are
 [`reports/figures/phase_7_dashboard.png`](reports/figures/phase_7_dashboard.png)
 and [`reports/figures/phase_7_predictor.png`](reports/figures/phase_7_predictor.png).
 
 The applicant form uses the configured 11-column raw model schema and calls
 the registered complete pipeline without fitting or duplicating preprocessing.
 Optional fields are passed as missing values for that pipeline's fitted
 imputers. The current model has no validated probability calibration, so the
 app displays its predicted historical class only. Its local explanation
 reports one-feature-at-a-time class sensitivity against training-partition
 medians/modes; this is descriptive, not causal or a lending rationale.
 
 ## Dependencies
 
 Runtime and test dependencies are version-pinned in `requirements.txt`; the
 project metadata and pytest configuration are in `pyproject.toml`.
 
 ## Data and modeling safeguards
 
 The labeled Kaggle loan data has been acquired and profiled separately from
 the unlabeled file. Candidate models use a stratified training/holdout split;
 all cross-validation fitting of imputation, encoding, scaling, and estimators
 occurs inside scikit-learn pipelines. Model selection used training-only CV
 balanced accuracy, with CV ROC-AUC as a tie-breaker, before the selected model
 was evaluated on the reserved holdout. No resampling is used; class weighting
 is applied within model fitting. The prediction application is intended to
 use a serialized pipeline fitted on training data.
 
 Dataset limitations, class balance, duplicate/overlapping records, evaluation
 metrics, and model limitations must be documented from observed data and
 measured results; none are assumed by this foundation.
 
 See [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) for package responsibilities,
 error handling, and planned application flow.
 
 The Kaggle source, acquisition details, and measured profiling summary are in
 [docs/dataset_source.md](docs/dataset_source.md). The detailed profile is
 saved as `artifacts/reports/dataset_profile.json`.
 
 The read-only data quality audit and interpretation are in
 `reports/data_quality_report.md`; raw CSVs are not modified by the audit.
 
 The training-data-only EDA notebook is
 [`notebooks/01_data_analysis.ipynb`](notebooks/01_data_analysis.ipynb). Run
 its cells top-to-bottom to regenerate `reports/figures/` and
 `reports/eda_report.md`. The notebook does not load the separate unlabeled
 Kaggle test CSV.
 
 The observed approval patterns, data limitations, feature considerations,
 preprocessing guidance, and potential demographic bias are discussed in
 [`reports/eda_insights.md`](reports/eda_insights.md). The report describes
 associations in the labeled sample and does not infer causation.
 
 The leakage-safe stratified split and fold-fitted transformation design are
 implemented in [`src/data/splitting.py`](src/data/splitting.py) and
 [`src/preprocessing/pipeline.py`](src/preprocessing/pipeline.py); usage and
 validation notes are in [`reports/preprocessing_report.md`](reports/preprocessing_report.md).
 
 Reusable income and loan feature engineering is implemented in
 [`src/features/engineering.py`](src/features/engineering.py) and runs inside
 the estimator pipeline. Its formulas, edge-case behavior, and test status are
 documented in [`reports/feature_engineering_report.md`](reports/feature_engineering_report.md).
 
 Model candidates and training workflow are implemented in
 [`src/models/classifiers.py`](src/models/classifiers.py) and
 [`src/models/train.py`](src/models/train.py). The executed workflow and its
 training-only cross-validation results are documented in
 [`reports/model_training_report.md`](reports/model_training_report.md). Run
 [`notebooks/03_model_training.ipynb`](notebooks/03_model_training.ipynb) to
 reproduce the training workflow; it does not evaluate the reserved holdout.
 
 Versioned complete pipelines are saved through the trusted local registry in
 [`src/models/registry.py`](src/models/registry.py). Loading requires registry

 # Intelligent Loan Approval & Credit Risk Prediction System
 
 An academic decision-support prototype for exploring loan approval and credit
 risk prediction. It is not an autonomous lending decision engine.
 
 ## Current phase
 
 Phases 0 through 7.3 are complete. The Streamlit predictor uses the registered
 v1.1.0 pipeline and configured 11-column applicant schema. It validates
 inputs, supports optional missing values, and provides class-only local
 sensitivity checks. Probability output remains disabled because calibration
 has not been validated.
 
 The Model Performance page reads saved candidate CV results and the Phase 5.1
 evaluation report. Holdout metrics and curves are explicitly labeled as
 baseline v1.0.0; tuned v1.1.0 is shown using training-only CV results because
 it has no holdout evaluation. Risk Analysis reads saved permutation-importance
 and fairness outputs plus historical group rates calculated from the labeled
 dataset. SHAP charts are shown only when saved outputs exist; otherwise the
 page displays the saved explainability status.
 
 ## Project layout
 
 ```text
 config.yaml             Central runtime configuration
 data/                   Raw, processed, and external data (private content ignored)
 notebooks/              Exploratory notebooks
 src/                    Configuration and domain-component packages
 app/                    Streamlit UI, pages, components, and services
 artifacts/               Generated model and report directories
 tests/                   Unit, integration, and validation tests
 docs/architecture.md    Architecture and responsibility boundaries
 logs/                   Local application logs (not committed)
 ```
 
 Configuration is loaded with `config.settings.load_config()`. The
 `loan_prediction.config` module remains as a compatibility import. Logging and
 random-seed helpers are in `utils/`.
 
 The root `config.yaml` owns dataset and artifact locations, split/CV settings,
 candidate model parameters, Streamlit page settings, and logging controls.
 `config.paths.ProjectPaths` resolves relative paths against the repository
 root, independent of the current working directory. Configuration validation
 fails with a `ConfigurationError` when required values are missing or invalid.
 Logs are emitted as structured JSON to the console and configured log file by
 default. Python and NumPy are seeded from `project.random_seed`; model
 estimators must use the same configured `project.random_seed` explicitly.
 
 ## Setup
 
 From the project root on Windows:
 
 ```powershell
 py -m venv env
 .\env\Scripts\Activate.ps1
 python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
 python -m pip install -e .
 ```
 
 ## Tests
 
 ```powershell
 python -m pytest
 ```
 
 ## Launch the Streamlit application
 
 ```powershell
 python -m streamlit run app.py
 ```
 
 The app includes a historical dashboard, an experimental prediction form,
 exploratory risk analysis, model-performance results, and project information.
 Historical dataset metrics and live browser-session predictions are kept
 separate. Predictions represent similarity to historical approval labels,
 not default or repayment risk.
 
 The UI palette is configured in `.streamlit/config.toml`; page styling and
 reusable UI components are in `app/components/`.
 
 The current UI screenshots are
 [`reports/figures/phase_7_dashboard.png`](reports/figures/phase_7_dashboard.png)
 and [`reports/figures/phase_7_predictor.png`](reports/figures/phase_7_predictor.png).
 Analytics screenshots:
 [`reports/figures/phase_7_model_performance.png`](reports/figures/phase_7_model_performance.png)
 and [`reports/figures/phase_7_risk_analysis.png`](reports/figures/phase_7_risk_analysis.png).
 
 The applicant form uses the configured 11-column raw model schema and calls
 the registered complete pipeline without fitting or duplicating preprocessing.
 Optional fields are passed as missing values for that pipeline's fitted
 imputers. The current model has no validated probability calibration, so the
 app displays its predicted historical class only. Its local explanation
 reports one-feature-at-a-time class sensitivity against training-partition
 medians/modes; this is descriptive, not causal or a lending rationale.
 
 ## Dependencies
 
 Runtime and test dependencies are version-pinned in `requirements.txt`; the
 project metadata and pytest configuration are in `pyproject.toml`.
 
 ## Data and modeling safeguards
 
 The labeled Kaggle loan data has been acquired and profiled separately from
 the unlabeled file. Candidate models use a stratified training/holdout split;
 all cross-validation fitting of imputation, encoding, scaling, and estimators
 occurs inside scikit-learn pipelines. Model selection used training-only CV
 balanced accuracy, with CV ROC-AUC as a tie-breaker, before the selected model
 was evaluated on the reserved holdout. No resampling is used; class weighting
 is applied within model fitting. The prediction application is intended to
 use a serialized pipeline fitted on training data.
 
 Dataset limitations, class balance, duplicate/overlapping records, evaluation
 metrics, and model limitations must be documented from observed data and
 measured results; none are assumed by this foundation.
 
 See [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) for package responsibilities,
 error handling, and planned application flow.
 
 The Kaggle source, acquisition details, and measured profiling summary are in
 [docs/dataset_source.md](docs/dataset_source.md). The detailed profile is
 saved as `artifacts/reports/dataset_profile.json`.
 
 The read-only data quality audit and interpretation are in
 `reports/data_quality_report.md`; raw CSVs are not modified by the audit.
 
 The training-data-only EDA notebook is
 [`notebooks/01_data_analysis.ipynb`](notebooks/01_data_analysis.ipynb). Run
 its cells top-to-bottom to regenerate `reports/figures/` and
 `reports/eda_report.md`. The notebook does not load the separate unlabeled
 Kaggle test CSV.
 
 The observed approval patterns, data limitations, feature considerations,
 preprocessing guidance, and potential demographic bias are discussed in
 [`reports/eda_insights.md`](reports/eda_insights.md). The report describes
 associations in the labeled sample and does not infer causation.
 
 The leakage-safe stratified split and fold-fitted transformation design are
 implemented in [`src/data/splitting.py`](src/data/splitting.py) and
 [`src/preprocessing/pipeline.py`](src/preprocessing/pipeline.py); usage and

 """Reusable CSV loading for separately labeled and unlabeled loan data."""
 
 import csv
 from dataclasses import dataclass
 from pathlib import Path
 from typing import Any
 
 import pandas as pd
 
 from config.paths import get_project_paths
 from config.settings import load_config, validate_config
 from data.validation import validate_dataset_pair
 from utils.exceptions import DataValidationError
 
 
 @dataclass(frozen=True)
 class DatasetBundle:
     """Labeled and unlabeled datasets loaded and validated independently."""
 
     labeled: pd.DataFrame
     unlabeled: pd.DataFrame
     target_column: str
     identifier_columns: tuple[str, ...]
 
 
 def load_csv(path: Path) -> pd.DataFrame:
     """Read one CSV file and reject unreadable or duplicate-header inputs."""
     path = Path(path)
     if not path.is_file():
         raise DataValidationError(f"Dataset file does not exist: {path}")
 
     try:
         with path.open(encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as csv_file:
             header = next(csv.reader(csv_file), None)

 class LoanFeatureEngineer(BaseEstimator, TransformerMixin):
     """Create income/loan features without learning from rows or target values.
 
     Missing, non-numeric, and non-finite numeric inputs are represented as
     ``NaN`` for downstream training-fold imputation. Ratios with nonpositive
     total income and log1p values outside the nonnegative domain are ``NaN``.
     Finite extreme values are not clipped using arbitrary or holdout-derived
     limits; non-finite results from arithmetic are converted to ``NaN``.
     """
 
     def __init__(
         self,
         numeric_columns: Sequence[str] = (
             "ApplicantIncome",
             "CoapplicantIncome",
             "LoanAmount",
             "Loan_Amount_Term",
         ),
         log1p_columns: Sequence[str] = (),
         excluded_columns: Sequence[str] = (),
     ) -> None:
         self.numeric_columns = numeric_columns
         self.log1p_columns = log1p_columns
         self.excluded_columns = excluded_columns
 
     def fit(
         self,
         X: pd.DataFrame,
         y: pd.Series | None = None,
     ) -> "LoanFeatureEngineer":
         """Validate required inputs without estimating any data statistics."""
         del y
         if not isinstance(X, pd.DataFrame):
             raise DataValidationError("Feature engineering input must be a DataFrame")
         required_columns = set(self.numeric_columns).union(
             {"ApplicantIncome", "CoapplicantIncome", "LoanAmount"}
         )
         missing_columns = sorted(required_columns.difference(X.columns))
         if missing_columns:
             raise DataValidationError(
                 f"Feature engineering input is missing required columns: "
                 f"{missing_columns}"
             )
         valid_log_columns = set(X.columns).union({"Total_Income"})
         invalid_log_columns = sorted(set(self.log1p_columns).difference(valid_log_columns))
         if invalid_log_columns:
             raise DataValidationError(
                 f"Cannot apply log1p to unconfigured feature columns: "
                 f"{invalid_log_columns}"
             )
         input_columns = X.drop(columns=list(self.excluded_columns), errors="ignore")
         self.feature_names_in_ = np.asarray(input_columns.columns, dtype=object)
         self.n_features_in_ = len(input_columns.columns)
         return self
 
     @staticmethod
     def _finite_numeric(series: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
         numeric = pd.to_numeric(series, errors="coerce").astype("float64")
         return numeric.where(np.isfinite(numeric), np.nan)
 
     def transform(self, X: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
         """Return sanitized inputs plus derived numeric features."""
         check_is_fitted(self, attributes=["feature_names_in_"])
         if not isinstance(X, pd.DataFrame):
             raise DataValidationError("Feature engineering input must be a DataFrame")
         transformed = X.drop(
             columns=list(self.excluded_columns),
             errors="ignore",
         ).copy()
         missing_columns = sorted(
             set(self.feature_names_in_).difference(transformed.columns)
         )
         if missing_columns:
             raise DataValidationError(
                 f"Feature engineering input is missing fitted columns: "
                 f"{missing_columns}"
             )
 
         for column in self.numeric_columns:
             transformed[column] = self._finite_numeric(transformed[column])
 
         with np.errstate(over="ignore", invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):

                 transformed["ApplicantIncome"] + transformed["CoapplicantIncome"]
             )

             transformed["Total_Income"] = total_income
 
             valid_ratio = (
                 transformed["Total_Income"].gt(0)
                 & transformed["LoanAmount"].ge(0)
             )
             ratio = transformed["LoanAmount"].div(
                 transformed["Total_Income"].where(valid_ratio)
             )
             transformed["Loan_to_Income_Ratio"] = ratio.where(
                 valid_ratio & np.isfinite(ratio), np.nan
             )
 
             for column in self.log1p_columns:
                 values = (
                     transformed["Total_Income"]
                     if column == "Total_Income"
                     else self._finite_numeric(transformed[column])
                 )
                 valid_log = values.ge(0)
                 logged = np.log1p(values.where(valid_log))
                 transformed[f"{column}_log1p"] = logged.where(
                     valid_log & np.isfinite(logged), np.nan
                 )
 
         return transformed.drop(
             columns=list(self.excluded_columns),
             errors="ignore",
         )
 
     def get_feature_names_out(
         self,
         input_features: Sequence[str] | None = None,
     ) -> np.ndarray:
         """Return names emitted by the transformation."""
         check_is_fitted(self, attributes=["feature_names_in_"])
         names = (
             list(input_features)
             if input_features is not None
             else list(self.feature_names_in_)
         )
         names.extend(["Total_Income", "Loan_to_Income_Ratio"])
         names.extend(f"{column}_log1p" for column in self.log1p_columns)
         return np.asarray(
             [name for name in names if name not in self.excluded_columns],
             dtype=object,
         )

 ) -> TrainingResult:

     to choose a model here. Each CV fold gets a fresh complete preprocessing
     and estimator pipeline. Candidate pipelines are finally refit on all

     classes = getattr(model, "classes_", None)
     if classes is None:
         raise ArtifactError("Selected model does not expose fitted class ordering")
     class_labels = list(classes)
     if POSITIVE_LABEL not in class_labels:
         raise ArtifactError(
             f"Selected model has no positive class {POSITIVE_LABEL!r}: {class_labels}"
         )
     probabilities = model.predict_proba(X)
     if probabilities.ndim != 2 or probabilities.shape[1] != len(class_labels):
         raise ArtifactError("Model probability output does not match class ordering")
     positive_index = class_labels.index(POSITIVE_LABEL)
     return np.asarray(probabilities[:, positive_index], dtype=float)

         float(tn / specificity_denominator)
         if specificity_denominator
