 # Intelligent Loan Approval & Credit Risk Prediction System
 
 An academic, reproducible machine-learning decision-support prototype for
 classifying historical loan approval labels. It is **not** an autonomous
 lending decision engine and does not predict repayment or default.
 
 ## Project overview
 
 ### Problem statement
 
 The public Kaggle dataset contains historical loan applications and an
 `Loan_Status` label. This project explores whether applicant information can
 classify the recorded label while preserving a leakage-safe modeling process,
 explainability limits, and a usable Streamlit interface.
 
 ### Objectives
 
 - Keep labeled training data separate from the Kaggle file without labels.
 - Audit and profile the input data without modifying the source CSVs.
 - Build reusable, fold-local preprocessing and feature engineering.
 - Compare four classifiers using the same stratified cross-validation folds.
 - Tune the selected candidate using training data only.
 - Record evaluation provenance and version complete model pipelines.
 - Explain model behavior and show the actual measured outputs in Streamlit.
 - Exercise the system with unit, integration, and validation tests.
 
 The target is the historical `Loan_Status` decision. A predicted `Y` is not a
 credit score, a probability of repayment, a default-risk category, or a
 recommendation to approve a loan.
 
 ## Scope and Limitations
 
 The model estimates whether an application resembles records historically
 labeled approved (`Y`) or rejected (`N`) in this dataset. It does not predict
 default, repayment, future borrower behavior, creditworthiness, or whether a
 real lender should approve an application. The available data has no verified
 default or repayment outcomes; no separate default or repayment model is
 implemented. Feature importance indicates predictive contribution within
 this dataset, not causation. The live application does not display class
 probabilities because calibration has not been validated.
 
 This output is an estimate of historical Loan_Status (approved/rejected), not default probability, repayment likelihood, a credit score, or a lending decision.
 
 ## Dataset and source
 
 Source: [Kaggle Loan Prediction Problem Dataset](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/altruistdelhite04/loan-prediction-problem-dataset).
 See [dataset acquisition notes](docs/dataset_source.md). The dataset license
 and reuse terms have not been independently verified; consult Kaggle before
 redistribution.
 
 The acquisition has two distinct files:
 
 | File | Rows | Columns | Role |
 |---|---:|---:|---|
 | `train_u6lujuX_CVtuZ9i.csv` | 614 | 13 | Labeled applications, including `Loan_Status` |
 | `test_Y3wMUE5_7gLdaTN.csv` | 367 | 12 | Unlabeled applications; never merged into training data |
 
 The labeled target distribution is 422 approvals (`Y`, 68.73%) and 192
 rejections (`N`, 31.27%). There are no duplicate rows, duplicate IDs, invalid
 target labels, or cross-file ID overlaps in the audited files. The labeled
 data has 50 missing `Credit_History` values (8.14%); other fields also contain
 missing values. Full field-level counts and the read-only quality audit are
 available in [the data-quality report](reports/data_quality_report.md) and
 [the dataset profile](artifacts/reports/dataset_profile.json).
 
 The CSVs are intentionally excluded from version control. Obtain the dataset
 from Kaggle and place the two files in `data/raw/` using the exact names above.
 No Kaggle credentials or download tokens are required by the loader.
 
 ## Data cleaning and preprocessing
 
 The quality audit does not delete records, impute values, or rewrite source
 files. It distinguishes domain violations from unusual but potentially valid
 observations; IQR flags are descriptive and do not automatically exclude
 applicants. No invalid categories, negative configured numeric values, or
 non-finite values were found in the acquired CSVs.
 
 For modeling:
 
 1. The target and identifier `Loan_ID` are excluded from model features.
 2. The labeled rows are split with stratification before fitting any learned
    transformation (configured holdout fraction 20%, seed 42).
 3. Each CV fold fits its own complete pipeline using median numeric
    imputation and scaling, categorical most-frequent imputation, and
    `OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore")`.
 4. Prediction-time validation requires exactly the configured 11 raw fields.
    Optional form values can be missing and pass through the same fitted
    pipeline. Unsupported categories are rejected by the form service; the
    underlying encoder itself ignores unseen categories.
 5. Class weighting / per-fit balanced sample weights are used rather than
    pre-split oversampling.
 
 ## Exploratory data analysis
 
 The EDA notebook reports numerical statistics, categorical distributions,
 income and loan amount distributions, loan term, credit history, employment
 status, approval/rejection counts, missingness, and numeric correlations. It
 used all 614 labeled source rows before the train/holdout split, including the
 123 rows later assigned to the holdout; therefore the holdout is not an
 independent confirmation set. It writes charts to `reports/figures/`. The
 observed association between credit-history group and historical approval is
 large (79.58% for value `1`; 7.87% for value `0`). Historical approval rates
 were 61.45% for Rural, 76.82% for Semiurban, and 65.84% for Urban
 applications. Applicant income medians were 3,833.5 for rejected and 3,812.5
 for approved records; loan amount medians were 129 and 126, respectively.
 These are sample summaries, not causal effects. Full context and the
 retrospective holdout disclosure are in [EDA insights](reports/eda_insights.md).
 
 ## Feature engineering
 
 `LoanFeatureEngineer` is applied inside the full training and inference
 pipeline. It creates:
 
 - `Total_Income = ApplicantIncome + CoapplicantIncome`
 - `Loan_to_Income_Ratio = LoanAmount / Total_Income`, when total income is
   positive and loan amount is nonnegative
 - Configured `log1p` features for nonnegative income and loan measurements
 
 Zero denominators, missing/non-numeric values, negative log inputs, and
 non-finite arithmetic are handled as missing values for subsequent
 training-fold imputation. Extreme finite source values are not clipped using
 arbitrary limits. **Loan-to-income ratio is not actual debt-to-income (DTI)**:
 the dataset does not include other debt obligations. More detail:
 [feature engineering report](reports/feature_engineering_report.md).
 
 ## Algorithms and measured comparison
 
 The candidate classifiers are Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random
 Forest, and Gradient Boosting. Candidate comparison uses 5-fold stratified
 CV on the 491-row training partition. Selection was by mean balanced accuracy,
 with mean ROC-AUC as a tie-breaker. The measured candidate CV means ± fold
 standard deviations are:
 
 | Candidate | Accuracy | Balanced accuracy | ROC-AUC | Specificity | Precision (Y) | Recall (Y) | F1 (Y) |
 |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
 | Logistic Regression | 0.723 ± 0.068 | 0.679 ± 0.074 | 0.743 ± 0.092 | 0.558 ± 0.117 | 0.799 ± 0.044 | 0.799 ± 0.079 | 0.797 ± 0.054 |
 | Decision Tree | 0.656 ± 0.060 | 0.631 ± 0.064 | 0.648 ± 0.076 | 0.565 ± 0.147 | 0.781 ± 0.047 | 0.697 ± 0.099 | 0.733 ± 0.058 |
 | Random Forest | 0.745 ± 0.061 | **0.684 ± 0.082** | **0.779 ± 0.072** | 0.520 ± 0.168 | 0.798 ± 0.052 | 0.849 ± 0.068 | 0.821 ± 0.042 |
 | Gradient Boosting | **0.768 ± 0.068** | 0.681 ± 0.088 | 0.734 ± 0.110 | 0.448 ± 0.153 | 0.785 ± 0.049 | **0.914 ± 0.054** | **0.844 ± 0.044** |
 
 The selected baseline was Random Forest v1.0.0. Training-only randomized
 search produced tuned Random Forest v1.1.0: balanced accuracy **0.6928 ±
 0.0635** and ROC-AUC **0.7828 ± 0.0601**, compared with baseline CV values
 0.6845 ± 0.0824 and 0.7787 ± 0.0724 on the same folds. The +0.0083 balanced
 accuracy difference is modest and not evidence by itself of a practically
 meaningful improvement.
 
 ### Holdout results — baseline v1.0.0 only
 
 The 123-row holdout results

 from pathlib import Path
 from typing import Any

 PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
 DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH = PROJECT_ROOT / "config.yaml"
 
 _PATH_SETTINGS = (

     "processed_data_dir",

     "raw_dataset",
     "labeled_dataset",
     "unlabeled_dataset",
     "processed_dataset",

 def _require_mapping(config: dict[str, Any], key: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
     value = config.get(key)
     if not isinstance(value, dict):
         raise ConfigurationError(f"Missing or invalid configuration section: {key}")
     return value
 
 
 def _require_nonempty_string(settings: dict[str, Any], key: str, section: str) -> str:
     value = settings.get(key)
     if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():
         raise ConfigurationError(f"Missing or invalid setting {section}.{key}")
     return value
 
 
 def validate_config(config: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
     """Validate all required settings and return the validated mapping.
 
     Raises:
         ConfigurationError: If a required section, setting, or value is invalid.
     """
     if not isinstance(config, dict):
         raise ConfigurationError("Configuration root must be a mapping")
 
     project = _require_mapping(config, "project")
     seed = project.get("random_seed")
     if (
         isinstance(seed, bool)
         or not isinstance(seed, int)
         or not 0 <= seed <= 2**32 - 1
     ):
         raise ConfigurationError(
             "project.random_seed must be an integer between 0 and 4294967295"
         )
     if not isinstance(project.get("deterministic"), bool):
         raise ConfigurationError("Missing or invalid setting project.deterministic")
     _require_nonempty_string(project, "name", "project")
 
     paths = _require_mapping(config, "paths")
     for key in _PATH_SETTINGS:
         _require_nonempty_string(paths, key, "paths")
 
     dataset = _require_mapping(config, "dataset")
     _require_nonempty_string(dataset, "source_url", "dataset")
     _require_nonempty_string(dataset, "target_column", "dataset")
     target_classes = dataset.get("target_classes")
     if (
         not isinstance(target_classes, list)
         or len(target_classes) < 2
         or any(not isinstance(value, str) or not value for value in target_classes)
         or len(set(target_classes)) != len(target_classes)
     ):

     identifier_columns = dataset.get("identifier_columns")
     if (
         not isinstance(identifier_columns, list)

     categorical_domains = dataset.get("categorical_domains")

     ):
         raise ConfigurationError(
             "dataset.categorical_domains must map column names to non-empty lists"
         )
     for key in ("numeric_columns", "positive_numeric_columns"):
         columns = dataset.get(key)
         if (
             not isinstance(columns, list)
             or any(not isinstance(column, str) or not column for column in columns)
         ):
             raise ConfigurationError(f"dataset.{key} must be a list of column names")
     if not set(dataset["positive_numeric_columns"]).issubset(
         dataset["numeric_columns"]
     ):
         raise ConfigurationError(
             "dataset.positive_numeric_columns must be a subset of numeric_columns"
         )
 
     feature_engineering = _require_mapping(config, "feature_engineering")
     log1p_columns = feature_engineering.get("log1p_columns")
     valid_log_columns = set(dataset["numeric_columns"]).union({"Total_Income"})

     training = _require_mapping(config, "training")

     if (

 """Model loading, input validation, and live approval prediction."""
 
 import json
 import warnings
 from typing import Any
 
 import numpy as np
 import pandas as pd
 
 from config.paths import get_project_paths
 from config.settings import load_config, validate_config
 from data.loader import load_csv
 from data.splitting import get_model_feature_columns, split_labeled_data
 from models.registry import load_model_artifact
 from prediction.scope import HISTORICAL_LOAN_STATUS_DISCLOSURE
 from utils.exceptions import DataValidationError
 
 
 def _load_training_features(settings: dict[str, Any]) -> pd.DataFrame:
     """Load only the configured training partition for form references."""
     paths = get_project_paths(settings)
     labeled_data = load_csv(paths.labeled_dataset)
     return split_labeled_data(labeled_data, config=settings).X_train
 
 
 def _reference_values(
     training_features: pd.DataFrame,
     settings: dict[str, Any],
 ) -> dict[str, Any]:
     """Calculate training-only medians and modes for display and explanations."""
     dataset = settings["dataset"]
     values: dict[str, Any] = {}
     for column in dataset["numeric_columns"]:
         values[column] = float(
             pd.to_numeric(training_features[column], errors="coerce").median()
         )
     for column in dataset["categorical_domains"]:
         modes = training_features[column].mode(dropna=True)
         if modes.empty:
             raise DataValidationError(
                 f"Cannot determine a training reference value for {column}"
             )
         values[column] = modes.iloc[0]
     return values
 
 
 def get_form_defaults(
     config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
 ) -> dict[str, Any]:
     """Compute editable examples from training-partition medians and modes."""
     settings = validate_config(config if config is not None else load_config())
     training_features = _load_training_features(settings)
     return _reference_values(training_features, settings)
 
 
 def load_prediction_model(
     config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
 ) -> tuple[Any, dict[str, Any]]:
     """Load and verify the configured local model and raw-feature schema."""
     settings = validate_config(config if config is not None else load_config())
     paths = get_project_paths(settings)
     dataset = load_csv(paths.labeled_dataset)
     feature_columns = get_model_feature_columns(settings)
     expected_schema = {column: str(dataset[column].dtype) for column in feature_columns}
     explainability = settings["explainability"]
     return load_model_artifact(
         model_name=explainability["model_name"],
         model_version=explainability["model_version"],
         model_dir=paths.models_dir,
         expected_feature_schema=expected_schema,
         expected_target_mapping={"N": 0, "Y": 1},
     )
 
 
 def predict_historical_approval(
     model: Any,
     applicant: dict[str, Any],
     config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
 ) -> dict[str, Any]:
     """Predict the historical approval class without exposing unvalidated scores."""
     settings = validate_config(config if config is not None else load_config())
     frame = _validated_applicant_row(applicant, settings)
     predicted_loan_status = _predict_class(model, frame, settings)
     return {
         "prediction_type": "historical_approval_prediction",
         "predicted_loan_status": predicted_loan_status,
         "model_name": settings["explainability"]["model_name"],
         "model_version": settings["explainability"]["model_version"],
         "target": "Loan_Status",
         "disclosure": HISTORICAL_LOAN_STATUS_DISCLOSURE,
     }
 
 
 def explain_historical_approval_prediction(
     model: Any,
     applicant: dict[str, Any],
     config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
 ) -> dict[str, Any]:
     """Report one-feature-at-a-time class sensitivity using training references.
 
     Replacing one input independently can create unrealistic combinations and
     does not establish a causal or additive explanation.
     """
     settings = validate_config(config if config is not None else load_config())
     feature_columns = get_model_feature_columns(settings)
     training_features = _load_training_features(settings)
     if list(training_features.columns) != list(feature_columns):
         raise DataValidationError(
             "Training reference schema does not match the prediction feature schema"
         )
 
     validated = _validated_applicant_row(applicant, settings)
     reference_values = _reference_values(training_features, settings)
     baseline = _predict_class(model, validated, settings)
     explanations: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
     for column in feature_columns:
         changed = validated.copy()
         changed.loc[0, column] = reference_values[column]
         changed_class = _predict_class(model, changed, settings)
         explanations.append(
             {
                 "feature": column,
                 "applicant_value": _display_value(validated.loc[0, column]),
                 "training_reference": _display_value(reference_values[column]),
                 "predicted_loan_status_after_replacement": changed_class,
                 "changed": changed_class != baseline,
             }
         )
     return {
         "prediction_type": "historical_approval_prediction",
         "predicted_loan_status": baseline,
         "method": "one-feature-at-a-time replacement with training median/mode",
         "reference_rows": int(len(training_features)),
         "features": explanations,
         "disclosure": HISTORICAL_LOAN_STATUS_DISCLOSURE,
         "warning": (
             "Descriptive model sensitivity only. Replacements can create "
             "unrealistic profiles and do not establish causation or an "
             "individual lending rationale."
         ),
     }
 
 
 def build_historical_prediction_exports(
     prediction: dict[str, Any],
     model_metadata: dict[str, Any],
 ) -> dict[str, str]:
     """Create downloadable JSON and CSV summaries without applicant inputs."""
     summary = {
         "prediction_type": "historical_approval_prediction",
         "target": "Loan_Status",
         "predicted_loan_status": prediction["predicted_loan_status"],
         "model_name": prediction["model_name"],
         "model_version": prediction["model_version"],
         "model_training_date": str(
             model_metadata.get("training_date", "unavailable")
         ),
         "disclosure": HISTORICAL_LOAN_STATUS_DISCLOSURE,
     }
     return {
         "json": json.dumps(summary, indent=2, ensure_ascii=True) + "\n",
         "csv": pd.DataFrame([summary]).to_csv(index=False),
     }

     applicant: dict[str, Any],

 ) -> pd.DataFrame:

     feature_columns = get_model_feature_columns(settings)
     missing = sorted(set(feature_columns).difference(applicant))
     extra = sorted(set(applicant).difference(feature_columns))

Objective:
Develop a real-world Machine Learning classification system that evaluates loan applications and predicts whether an applicant is likely to be approved or pose a default/credit risk based on financial, employment, and demographic attributes.

Tech Stack & Tools:

 • Language: Python

 • Libraries: Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn, Matplotlib / Seaborn

 • Environment: Jupyter Notebook (.ipynb) or Google Colab (plus optional modular .py scripts)

Core Requirements:

1. Dataset Selection:

 • Use a standard public Loan Prediction / Credit Risk dataset (such as the Loan Prediction Problem Dataset from Kaggle) and document the dataset source/link.

2. Data Cleaning & Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA):

 • Handle missing values, duplicate rows, and skewed numerical features (e.g., applicant income, loan amount).

 • Perform categorical encoding and feature scaling/engineering (such as creating a Total_Income or Debt_to_Income ratio).

 • Generate at least 3–4 clear visualizations illustrating key approval vs. rejection patterns.

3. Model Training & Comparison:

 • Train and compare at least 3 classification models (e.g., Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Decision Tree, Gradient Boosting / XGBoost).

# MASTER DEVELOPMENT PROMPT — Loan Default and Credit Risk Prediction Module
You are working on an existing Intelligent Loan Approval and Credit Risk Prediction System built with Python, Scikit-learn, and Streamlit.

Your task is to develop a new, independent Loan Default and Credit Risk Prediction module using genuine historical loan repayment data.

The existing historical loan approval classifier must remain functional and unchanged.

# 1. Dataset Acquisition — Mandatory
Use the following public dataset as the primary source:

**Primary dataset: LendingClub Loan Data**

Kaggle download page:
[https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/wordsforthewise/lending-club](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/wordsforthewise/lending-club)

Dataset source:
[https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/wordsforthewise/lending-club](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/wordsforthewise/lending-club)

This dataset contains historical LendingClub loan records, including loan performance information and repayment outcomes.

**Alternative dataset, if the primary dataset cannot be acquired or validated:**

Give Me Some Credit:
[https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/GiveMeSomeCredit](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/GiveMeSomeCredit)

This alternative contains the target `SeriousDlqin2yrs`, representing serious delinquency within two years.

Do not combine these datasets into one training dataset. Select one dataset, document the decision, and build the initial model using that dataset only.

## Dataset acquisition instructions

1. Open the primary Kaggle dataset link.
2. Inspect its available files, descriptions, columns, and licensing conditions.
3. Download the dataset if access is available.
4. If automatic download is unavailable, provide clear instructions for manually downloading and placing the files in the project.
5. Support Kaggle API download only when the user has configured valid credentials.
6. Never hardcode or expose Kaggle credentials.
7. Verify the downloaded files before using them.
8. Record the original source, download date, filename, and dataset version where available.
Create a dataset folder such as:

`data/default_risk/raw/`

Store cleaned and processed data separately:

`data/default_risk/processed/`

Do not overwrite the existing historical approval dataset.

# 2. Inspect and Validate Dataset
Before model development, inspect:

- Number of records.
- Available columns.
- Data types.
- Missing values.
- Duplicate records.
- Target variable.
- Class distribution.
- Date coverage.
- Loan performance status.
- Data quality issues.
Identify which columns are available at the intended loan application prediction time.

Create a dataset audit report.

Do not assume that every dataset column is appropriate for prediction.

# 3. Define Default Prediction Target
For LendingClub, inspect the actual loan status values and official dataset descriptions.

Develop a documented binary target using appropriate historical outcomes.

Possible mapping, subject to validation against the dataset documentation:

- `Charged Off` = Default class.
- `Fully Paid` = Non-default class.
Evaluate other statuses separately.

Do not automatically classify:

- Current loans.
- Late loans.
- In Grace Period loans.
- Incomplete outcomes.
- Unknown outcomes.
as either fully repaid or defaulted.

Exclude unresolved outcomes from the initial binary training target unless a defensible alternative methodology is documented.

Document the exact mapping and its limitations.

If using Give Me Some Credit instead, use `SeriousDlqin2yrs` as the target and follow its documented definition.

Never use `Loan_Status` from the existing historical approval dataset as a default target.

# 4. Prevent Data Leakage
Create a strict feature eligibility policy.

Exclude post-origination information that would not be available at the intended prediction time, including:

- Actual payment amounts.
- Final loan status.
- Recovery amounts.
- Collection activity.
- Charge-off dates.
- Future delinquency information.
- Post-loan repayment records.
Inspect all columns and document every excluded feature and the reason for exclusion.

Use time-based validation where reliable loan dates are available.

If the dataset has a defined observation period, document the prediction horizon and the limitations of the available data.

# 5. Data Engineering
Create a separate default-risk data pipeline.

Implement:

- Data profiling.
- Missing-value handling.
- Duplicate detection.
- Outlier analysis.
- Categorical encoding.
- Numerical scaling where appropriate.
- Feature engineering.
- Class imbalance analysis.
- Target validation.
Use Scikit-learn Pipeline and ColumnTransformer.

Fit preprocessing only on training data.

Do not perform SMOTE or other resampling before splitting.

# 6. Model Development
Train and compare at least four models:

- Logistic Regression.
- Decision Tree.
- Random Forest.
- Gradient Boosting or XGBoost, if justified.
Use:

- Training-only cross-validation.
- Appropriate class imbalance handling.
- Consistent feature sets.
- Reproducible random seeds.
- Suitable validation splits.
Do not use the final test set for model selection or tuning.

# 7. Model Evaluation
Calculate:

- Accuracy.
- Precision.
- Recall.
- F1-score.
- ROC-AUC.
- PR-AUC.
- Specificity.
- Balanced accuracy.
- Confusion matrix.
- Brier score.
- Log loss.
Prioritize default-class recall and precision-recall trade-offs.

Explain why accuracy alone can be misleading for imbalanced datasets.

Keep the final test set untouched until final evaluation.

# 8. Calibration and Risk Categories
Where appropriate:

- Evaluate probability calibration.
- Use training-only cross-validation.
- Compare calibrated and uncalibrated probabilities.
- Use configurable risk thresholds.
- Document the methodology used to select thresholds.
Create configurable categories:

- Low Risk.
- Moderate Risk.
- High Risk.
- Very High Risk.
Do not present illustrative thresholds as universal banking standards.

# 9. Explainability
Implement:

- Global feature importance.
- Permutation importance.
- SHAP, if suitable and computationally feasible.
- Individual prediction explanations.
Explain which features contributed to higher or lower estimated default probability.

Do not describe feature importance as proof of causation.

# 10. Application Integration
Create a separate Streamlit page:

**Loan Default Risk Prediction**

Include:

- Loan and applicant information.
- Estimated default probability.
- Estimated non-default probability.
- Risk category.
- Important contributing factors.
- Model version.
- Dataset information.
- Prediction limitations.
Do not reuse the historical Loan_Status classifier.

# 11. Model Registry
Register the new default-risk model separately.

Save:

- Model identifier.
- Model version.
- Dataset source.
- Dataset fingerprint.
- Target definition.
- Feature list.
- Training date.
- Evaluation metrics.
- Calibration configuration.
- Preprocessing configuration.
Use the existing trusted artifact registry where appropriate.

# 12. Testing
Test:

- Dataset acquisition and validation.
- Target mapping.
- Exclusion of unresolved loan outcomes.
- Leakage prevention.
- Feature eligibility.
- Preprocessing.
- Model training.
- Probability outputs.
- Calibration.
- Risk category assignment.
- Artifact saving and loading.
- Streamlit inference integration.
- Invalid and missing inputs.

# 13. Mandatory Disclaimer
Display this statement on the new module:

"This output is a statistical estimate of loan default risk based on historical loan performance data. It is not a guarantee of future repayment or default, a regulated credit rating, or an automatic lending decision."

# 14. Deliverables
Create:

- Dataset acquisition documentation.
- Dataset audit report.
- Target definition documentation.
- Feature eligibility documentation.
- Default-risk training pipeline.
- Model evaluation report.
- Calibration report.
- Explainability report.
- Default-risk model artifact.
- Model metadata.
- Streamlit page.
- Automated tests.
- README updates.

# 15. Final Implementation Report
Report:

1. Dataset downloaded and source link.
2. Files acquired and their locations.
3. Dataset size and quality.
4. Target definition and class distribution.
5. Features included and excluded.
6. Leakage prevention methods.
7. Models trained.
8. Evaluation results.
9. Calibration results.
10. Explainability implementation.
11. Files created or modified.
12. Tests executed and actual results.
13. Remaining limitations.
Use PASS, PARTIAL, FAIL, or NOT IMPLEMENTED with evidence.

If the dataset cannot be downloaded or validated, stop before model training and explain what is missing.

Do not fabricate dataset records, repayment labels, or evaluation results.

Do not claim that default prediction has been implemented until a model has been trained and evaluated using genuine loan repayment/default outcomes.

                 "Late": "excluded_unresolved",
                 "In Grace Period": "excluded_unresolved",
                 "Default": "excluded_unresolved",
             },
         },
         "givemecredit": {
             "target_column": {"SeriousDlqin2yrs": "SeriousDlqin2yrs"},
             "default_label": {"1": "default"},
             "non_default_label": {"0": "non_default"},
             "excluded_statuses": {},
         },
     }
 
 
 def evaluate_default_risk_dataset(project_root: Path | str) -> DefaultRiskDatasetStatus:
     """Report whether a default-risk dataset is available for training.
 
     The default-risk module stays intentionally inactive until a genuine
     repayment/default dataset has been downloaded and validated. This function
     only checks file availability and project layout; it never invents labels.
     """
     root = Path(project_root)
     dataset_dir = root / "data" / "default_risk"
     raw_dir = dataset_dir / "raw"
     processed_dir = dataset_dir / "processed"
 
     missing_requirements: list[str] = []
     if not dataset_dir.exists():
         missing_requirements.append("data/default_risk directory is missing")
     if not raw_dir.exists():
         missing_requirements.append("data/default_risk/raw directory is missing")
     if not processed_dir.exists():
         missing_requirements.append("data/default_risk/processed directory is missing")
 
     raw_files = sorted(path.name for path in raw_dir.glob("*.csv")) if raw_dir.exists() else []
     if not raw_files:
         missing_requirements.append(
             "No raw CSV dataset file found for LendingClub or Give Me Some Credit"
         )
 
     if missing_requirements:
         return DefaultRiskDatasetStatus(
             dataset_name="lendingclub_or_givemecredit",
             status="NOT_AVAILABLE",
             dataset_dir=str(dataset_dir),
             raw_files=raw_files,
             missing_requirements=missing_requirements,
             notes=(
                 "The default-risk module is intentionally blocked until the "
                 "source repayment dataset has been downloaded and validated. "
                 "This module is not trained and no default-risk model is produced "
                 "without genuine default labels."
             ),
         )
 
     return DefaultRiskDatasetStatus(
         dataset_name="lendingclub_or_givemecredit",
         status="READY",
         dataset_dir=str(dataset_dir),
         raw_files=raw_files,
         missing_requirements=[],
         notes=(
             "A default-risk dataset is present. A complete target-definition, "
             "feature-eligibility, and training audit must still be executed before "
             "model training."
         ),
     )

     "DefaultRiskDatasetStatus",
     "evaluate_default_risk_dataset",
     "get_default_risk_target_mapping",
 ]

 # Intelligent Loan Approval & Credit Risk Prediction System
 
 An academic, reproducible machine-learning decision-support prototype for
 classifying historical loan approval labels. It is **not** an autonomous
 lending decision engine and does not predict repayment or default.
 
 ## Project overview
 
 ### Problem statement
 
 The public Kaggle dataset contains historical loan applications and an
 `Loan_Status` label. This project explores whether applicant information can
 classify the recorded label while preserving a leakage-safe modeling process,
 explainability limits, and a usable Streamlit interface.
 
 ### Objectives
 
 - Keep labeled training data separate from the Kaggle file without labels.
 - Audit and profile the input data without modifying the source CSVs.
 - Build reusable, fold-local preprocessing and feature engineering.
 - Compare four classifiers using the same stratified cross-validation folds.
 - Tune the selected candidate using training data only.
 - Record evaluation provenance and version complete model pipelines.
 - Explain model behavior and show the actual measured outputs in Streamlit.
 - Exercise the system with unit, integration, and validation tests.
 
 The target is the historical `Loan_Status` decision. A predicted `Y` is not a
 credit score, a probability of repayment, a default-risk category, or a
 recommendation to approve a loan.
 
 ## Scope and Limitations
 
 The model estimates whether an application resembles records historically
 labeled approved (`Y`) or rejected (`N`) in this dataset. It does not predict
 default, repayment, future borrower behavior, creditworthiness, or whether a
 real lender should approve an application. The available data has no verified
 default or repayment outcomes; no separate default or repayment model is
 implemented. Feature importance indicates predictive contribution within
 this dataset, not causation. The live application does not display class
 probabilities because calibration has not been validated.
 
 This output is an estimate of historical Loan_Status (approved/rejected), not default probability, repayment likelihood, a credit score, or a lending decision.
 
 ## Default-risk module status
 
 A separate loan default and credit risk prediction module is intentionally not trained in this repository yet. The project remains scoped to the historical `Loan_Status` approval classifier unless a valid repayment/default dataset is first downloaded and audited.
 
 The primary dataset target for a genuine default-risk module is LendingClub loan performance data, with `Charged Off` mapped to the default class and `Fully Paid` mapped to the non-default class, while unresolved statuses such as current or grace-period loans are excluded from the initial supervised target. The alternative target is `SeriousDlqin2yrs` from the Give Me Some Credit dataset. No model training is performed until one dataset is acquired, validated, and documented in `data/default_risk/`.
 
 This repository currently does not contain the required LendingClub or Give Me Some Credit files under `data/default_risk/raw/`, so no default-risk model, probability outputs, or risk categories are being claimed as implemented.
 
 ## Dataset and source
 
 Source: [Kaggle Loan Prediction Problem Dataset](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/altruistdelhite04/loan-prediction-problem-dataset).
 See [dataset acquisition notes](docs/dataset_source.md). The dataset license
 and reuse terms have not been independently verified; consult Kaggle before
 redistribution.
 
 The acquisition has two distinct files:
 
 | File | Rows | Columns | Role |
 |---|---:|---:|---|
 | `train_u6lujuX_CVtuZ9i.csv` | 614 | 13 | Labeled applications, including `Loan_Status` |
 | `test_Y3wMUE5_7gLdaTN.csv` | 367 | 12 | Unlabeled applications; never merged into training data |
 
 The labeled target distribution is 422 approvals (`Y`, 68.73%) and 192
 rejections (`N`, 31.27%). There are no duplicate rows, duplicate IDs, invalid
 target labels, or cross-file ID overlaps in the audited files. The labeled
 data has 50 missing `Credit_History` values (8.14%); other fields also contain
 missing values. Full field-level counts and the read-only quality audit are
 available in [the data-quality report](reports/data_quality_report.md) and
 [the dataset profile](artifacts/reports/dataset_profile.json).
 
 The CSVs are intentionally excluded from version control. Obtain the dataset
 from Kaggle and place the two files in `data/raw/` using the exact names above.
 No Kaggle credentials or download tokens are required by the loader.
 
 ## Data cleaning and preprocessing
 
 The quality audit does not delete records, impute values, or rewrite source
 files. It distinguishes domain violations from unusual but potentially valid
 observations; IQR flags are descriptive and do not automatically exclude
 applicants. No invalid categories, negative configured numeric values, or
 non-finite values were found in the acquired CSVs.
